metaTitle: Abu Dhabi to Dubai Airport: How Early Should You Leave?
metaDescription: Leave Abu Dhabi five hours before a DXB departure: around 90 minutes on the road plus the three hours Dubai Airports asks for. Terminals, tolls and pitfalls.
excerpt: Leave Abu Dhabi five hours before your flight from Dubai International, or four and a half hours off-peak with hand luggage only. That covers a 90 minute to two hour drive and the three hours Dubai Airports recommends in the terminal. Here is how the timing breaks down, which terminal to give your chauffeur, and what catches people out.
quickAnswer: Leave Abu Dhabi five hours before your flight departs from Dubai International (DXB). The drive takes around 90 minutes on a clear road and up to two hours in peak traffic, and Dubai Airports asks passengers to arrive at least three hours before departure. With online check-in, hand luggage only and an off-peak flight, four and a half hours is the minimum worth risking.
content:
Leave Abu Dhabi five hours before your flight departs from Dubai International (DXB), and no later than four and a half hours before if you are travelling off-peak with hand luggage only. The drive takes around 90 minutes on a clear road and closer to two hours in rush hour, and Dubai Airports asks you to be in the terminal at least three hours before departure. Add the two together and you have your leaving time.

That sounds generous until you have sat on Sheikh Zayed Road at 5pm on a Thursday. This guide walks through the numbers behind that answer, what the airport and the airlines actually ask of you, and the handful of things that catch people out on this route.

How early should you leave Abu Dhabi for a flight from Dubai Airport?

Five hours before departure is the safe answer for an international flight with checked bags. Work backwards from the departure time: three hours in the terminal, plus 90 minutes to two hours on the road, plus a short buffer for a bad-luck moment such as a slow bridge crossing or an accident on the E11.

Four and a half hours works if you are checked in online, carrying hand luggage only, and your flight leaves outside the morning or evening peak. Any less than that and you are betting on traffic, and traffic between the two cities does not care about your boarding time.

What should you have ready before the car arrives?

The delays on this transfer tend to happen before the car has moved. Have these sorted the night before and the pickup itself takes two minutes.

  • Your flight number and scheduled departure time, so the pickup can be timed correctly
  • The terminal you are flying from (DXB has three, and they are not next to each other)
  • Online check-in done, with the boarding pass saved to your phone
  • Passport and any visa or residency documents in your hand luggage, not the checked bag
  • Bags packed and by the door, with the count matching the vehicle you booked
  • Child seat requested at booking if you are travelling with small children
  • Your pickup address pinned accurately, especially in villa compounds and hotel complexes with several entrances

How long does the drive from Abu Dhabi to Dubai Airport take?

Around 90 minutes from central Abu Dhabi to DXB is the honest working figure. The route runs along Sheikh Zayed Road (the E11) or Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road (the E311), both of which the UAE Government portal lists as the main arteries linking Abu Dhabi to Dubai and the northern emirates.

Three things stretch that time. The first is the morning peak into Dubai and the evening peak out of it, when the last stretch past Jebel Ali and through the city can crawl. The second is leaving Abu Dhabi island itself, because every route off the island funnels over one of four bridges.

The third is your starting point. Saadiyat, Yas Island and the airport side of the city sit closer to the Dubai road than the Corniche or Al Bateen, and the difference can be 20 minutes before you have even joined the motorway. Emirates Limo runs private transfers from Abu Dhabi to Dubai around the clock, so the chauffeur knows which of those starting points needs the extra margin.

What time does Dubai Airport want you in the terminal?

Three hours before departure, according to Dubai Airports, which also notes that check-in counters open at approximately that point. That three hours is the figure to build your plan around, whichever airline you fly.

Emirates goes further and breaks it down. Its check-in guidance says to be through passport control and security 90 minutes before departure, at the gate 60 minutes before in Economy, and allows up to 25 minutes to walk to the C gates at Terminal 3.

The airport figure is the one to plan with, but the airline figure tells you where the time goes once you are inside. Check-in, immigration, security and the walk to the gate are four separate queues, and DXB is a big place on a busy evening.

Which Dubai Airport terminal are you flying from?

Get the terminal wrong and you can lose 30 to 40 minutes at the worst possible moment. DXB has three terminals on different sides of the airfield, and moving between them by road means leaving the airport and re-entering.

Emirates flights use Emirates Terminal 3, with gates in Concourses A, B and C. Other airlines use Terminal 1 or Terminal 2, and your ticket or the airline's app will say which.

Give the terminal at booking and the chauffeur drops you at the departures level entrance for that terminal. Dubai Airports has designated drop-off areas at each terminal with a parking time limit, so the handover is quick: bags out, a handshake, and you are through the doors.

Do you pay tolls on the Abu Dhabi to Dubai road?

Yes, two systems apply, and neither is something you deal with in the car. Abu Dhabi's Darb gates sit on the four bridges leading to Abu Dhabi city, and Dubai's Salik gates sit on the main roads through Dubai, both documented on the UAE Government portal.

Darb charges AED 4 per crossing during peak hours and nothing outside them, while Salik is charged at each gate a vehicle passes. A chauffeur car carries its own tag and registration, so there is no cash to hand over and no fine landing on you later.

The number that matters more to you is the one on your booking confirmation. Emirates Limo fixes the fare at the moment you book, and there is no surge pricing and no extra charge if traffic adds 30 minutes to the run.

What goes wrong on an Abu Dhabi to Dubai Airport transfer?

The same four things, over and over. All of them are avoidable with a few minutes of care at booking.

A pickup time set from the departure time, not from the road. People book a 6pm pickup for a 9pm flight because three hours sounds right, forgetting the drive is inside those three hours. Set the pickup five hours before departure and let the chauffeur be early rather than you being late.

The wrong terminal. "Dubai Airport" is not enough on a booking form when three terminals are involved. Put the terminal and the airline on the booking and the chauffeur will confirm it on the way.

A late change of plan. A flight moved by the airline, a second passenger added, or a pickup shifted from a hotel to an office all need the booking updated. Emirates Limo gives a full refund for a cancellation made 24 hours or more before pickup, and no refund inside 24 hours, so the earlier you tell us, the more options you have.

Not being at the door. Free waiting time on a pickup away from the airport is 15 minutes. If your bags are still upstairs at the pickup time, that buffer disappears before the car has moved.

Is a private chauffeur worth it for this route?

For an airport run with a hard deadline, yes, and the reason is control. You choose the leaving time, the car is reserved for you alone, and the price is fixed before the journey starts.

OptionTiming you controlWhat can go wrong
Private chauffeurPickup time booked in advance, chauffeur waits at your doorVery little, provided the pickup time allows for traffic
Street taxiDepends on finding one at your location at the right momentAvailability at peak times, meter runs in traffic, driver may need directions to the terminal
Self-drive rentalFully yoursReturning the car at DXB, parking, tolls and fuel add time and steps at the end

Group size settles the vehicle choice. A sedan such as the Lexus ES300 carries four passengers and three bags, a GMC Yukon carries six passengers and six bags, and the Emirates Limo fleet page lists the full range with capacities.

Flying in the other direction later? The same team runs the Dubai airport transfer for arrivals, meeting you in the arrivals hall with a name board, tracking the flight and including 60 minutes of free waiting time from landing.

What is the simplest way to set the pickup time?

Take your departure time, subtract five hours, and that is your pickup. For a 2pm flight, book the car for 9am; for a 9pm flight, book it for 4pm.

If you are checked in online with hand luggage only and the flight is well outside the peaks, you can trim to four and a half hours. Do not trim further to save 30 minutes at home, because that 30 minutes is worth far more at the airport than on the sofa.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get from Abu Dhabi to Dubai Airport?
faqs.answer: Around 90 minutes from central Abu Dhabi to Dubai International on a clear road, and closer to two hours in the morning or evening peak. The route follows the E11 or E311, and leaving Abu Dhabi island over one of the four bridges adds time at busy periods.

faqs.question: How many hours before my flight should I be at Dubai Airport?
faqs.answer: At least three hours before departure, which is the figure Dubai Airports gives in its own FAQs. Check-in counters open at roughly the same point. Emirates adds that you should be through passport control and security 90 minutes before departure and at the gate 60 minutes before in Economy.

faqs.question: Which terminal at DXB does Emirates use?
faqs.answer: Emirates uses Emirates Terminal 3 at Dubai International, with gates in Concourses A, B and C. Other airlines use Terminal 1 or Terminal 2. Give the terminal at booking so the chauffeur drops you at the correct departures entrance, because the terminals are on different sides of the airfield.

faqs.question: Are tolls included in an Abu Dhabi to Dubai airport transfer?
faqs.answer: The price you see at booking is the price you pay. Emirates Limo fixes the fare at the moment of booking, with no surge pricing and no extra charge for traffic or flight delays, and nothing is collected in the car.

faqs.question: Can I cancel an Emirates Limo transfer if my flight changes?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a full refund if you cancel 24 hours or more before the pickup time. Cancellations inside 24 hours of pickup, and no-shows, are charged in full. If the airline moves your flight, tell Emirates Limo as early as possible so the pickup time can be adjusted.
